# Pick & place cell -- TIA Portal starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The function block's body is yours.*

**The task.** Sequence three motions against feedback, not timers. Ramp the infeed drive, read each carton's code at the scanner, then travel · lower · grip · raise · travel · release to put it on the outfeed. The gantry reports whether the vacuum actually caught anything.

**Done when.** Every carton fed reaches the outfeed, and gantry.holding is true on every carry — a cycle that runs with holding false carried air. Careful with inposition: a target written this scan does not reach the machine until the next one, so on the scan that issues a move it still reports the place you are trying to leave.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`pick_and_place_cell.scl`](pick_and_place_cell.scl) | SCL source: the global DB `FF_IO` with every signal, and an empty FB `"PickAndPlaceCell"`. |
| [`opcua_mapping.json`](opcua_mapping.json) | For `--driver opcua-client`: tag id -> `ns=3;s="FF_IO"."..."`. |
| [`snap7_mapping.json`](snap7_mapping.json) | For `--driver s7-snap7`: tag id -> `DBX`/`DBD` offset in `FF_IO`. |
| [`plcsim_mapping.json`](plcsim_mapping.json) | For `--driver plcsim-advanced`: tag id -> `FF_IO.<Name>`. |

The Siemens walkthrough -- PLCSIM Advanced, the OPC UA server, finding
NodeIds -- is [`../README.md`](../README.md). This page is only what is
different about this scene.

## Set it up

1. In a project with an S7-1500 CPU: *External source files -> Add new
   external file*, pick `pick_and_place_cell.scl`, then right-click it -> *Generate
   blocks from source*. That creates `FF_IO` and `"PickAndPlaceCell"`. One
   exercise per CPU: this `FF_IO` replaces any other one.
2. Call `"PickAndPlaceCell"` from OB1 (drag it into `Main`; TIA creates the
   instance DB).
3. Check `FF_IO`'s properties: *Optimized block access* off (the source sets
   it), *Accessible from HMI/OPC UA* and *Writable from HMI/OPC UA* on for
   every member (TIA's default). Without *Writable* every sensor reads FALSE
   forever.
4. Compile, download, RUN.

## Run it

Open the scene in FactoryForge first (pick "Pick & place cell" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/pick_and_place_cell.json)), then attach
the sidecar with whichever driver reaches your CPU, in the folder
FactoryForge was extracted to:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver opcua-client --mapping examples/tia/pick-and-place-cell/opcua_mapping.json -o url opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver s7-snap7 -o host <cpu-ip> -o db <FF_IO's number> --mapping examples/tia/pick-and-place-cell/snap7_mapping.json
.\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver plcsim-advanced -o instance <name> --mapping examples/tia/pick-and-place-cell/plcsim_mapping.json
```

On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. To have it marked, stop the sidecar and
start the grader in place of the 3D scene, in one terminal:

```
.\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene pick-and-place-cell
```

then run the same `connect` command in a second terminal with the bus port
the grader printed added: `--port <bus port it printed>`.

<!-- from-source -->
(From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar` in place of
`.\factoryforge-sidecar`, with the sidecar installed and run from the repository
root so the paths resolve.)
<!-- /from-source -->

The OPC UA namespace index is usually 3, not always: run
`.\factoryforge-sidecar browse opc.tcp://<cpu-ip>:4840` once and fix `ns=` in
the mapping if yours differs.

## FF_IO

In declaration order. `PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp);
`PLC reads` is an input (a sensor, a button, a measurement). The two
directions never share a byte, so the snap7 driver never rewrites a bit your
program owns. `FF_IO` is 36 bytes. *Brief* marks the signals the task
names.

| Tag | Direction | Member | Type | Offset | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gantry.target` | PLC writes | `GantryTarget` | Real | DBD0 | rail position to travel to, 0..100 % of the 2.4 m rail | yes |
| `infeed.speed` | PLC writes | `InfeedSpeed` | Real | DBD4 | speed reference, 0..100 % of 0.8 m/s; the drive ramps towards it | yes |
| `rate.value` | PLC writes | `RateValue` | Real | DBD8 | needle position, scale 0..100 % |  |
| `alarm.beacon` | PLC writes | `AlarmBeacon` | Bool | DBX12.0 | rotating alarm beacon |  |
| `alarm.horn` | PLC writes | `AlarmHorn` | Bool | DBX12.1 | alarm horn |  |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | `EmitterEmit` | Bool | DBX12.2 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll; every 4th carton is steel |  |
| `gantry.grip` | PLC writes | `GantryGrip` | Bool | DBX12.3 | vacuum on | yes |
| `gantry.lower` | PLC writes | `GantryLower` | Bool | DBX12.4 | lower the cup (FALSE raises it) | yes |
| `infeed.run` | PLC writes | `InfeedRun` | Bool | DBX12.5 | run the drive | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | `PanelGreen` | Bool | DBX12.6 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | `PanelRed` | Bool | DBX12.7 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `pickstation.rotate` | PLC writes | `PickstationRotate` | Bool | DBX13.0 | run the belt |  |
| `scanner.enable` | PLC writes | `ScannerEnable` | Bool | DBX13.1 | arm the reader; FALSE switches it off -- and an output you never write is FALSE | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | `TowerGreen` | Bool | DBX13.2 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | `TowerRed` | Bool | DBX13.3 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | `TowerYellow` | Bool | DBX13.4 | tower lamp, yellow |  |
| `gantry.position` | PLC reads | `GantryPosition` | Real | DBD14 | rail position now, 0..100 % | yes |
| `infeed.actual` | PLC reads | `InfeedActual` | Real | DBD18 | actual speed, % -- lags the reference while the drive ramps | yes |
| `outfeed.count` | PLC reads | `OutfeedCount` | DInt | DBD22 | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | `PanelSetpoint` | Real | DBD26 | the operator's pot, 10..100 % (starts at 60) |  |
| `scanner.code` | PLC reads | `ScannerCode` | DInt | DBD30 | last code read, held until the next: 101 short, 102 tall, 201 metal | yes |
| `atstation.detect` | PLC reads | `AtstationDetect` | Bool | DBX34.0 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam |  |
| `gantry.fault` | PLC reads | `GantryFault` | Bool | DBX34.1 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted |  |
| `gantry.holding` | PLC reads | `GantryHolding` | Bool | DBX34.2 | the vacuum really has a carton (not just: grip is on) | yes |
| `gantry.inposition` | PLC reads | `GantryInposition` | Bool | DBX34.3 | within 1.5 % of the target it holds NOW -- stale on the scan you change the target | yes |
| `gantry.lowered` | PLC reads | `GantryLowered` | Bool | DBX34.4 | cup fully down | yes |
| `gantry.raised` | PLC reads | `GantryRaised` | Bool | DBX34.5 | cup fully up | yes |
| `infeed.fault` | PLC reads | `InfeedFault` | Bool | DBX34.6 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn |  |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | `PanelEstop` | Bool | DBX34.7 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | `PanelReset` | Bool | DBX35.0 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press |  |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | `PanelStart` | Bool | DBX35.1 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | `PanelStop` | Bool | DBX35.2 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `pickstation.fault` | PLC reads | `PickstationFault` | Bool | DBX35.3 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `scanner.present` | PLC reads | `ScannerPresent` | Bool | DBX35.4 | TRUE while a carton is under the reader | yes |
| `scanner.read` | PLC reads | `ScannerRead` | Bool | DBX35.5 | TRUE for 0.2 s on each new read, as `code` changes -- latch the code on the rising edge | yes |

`int` travels as a `DInt` and `float` as a `Real`: the OPC UA driver writes
Int32 and Float, and a member of any other type is refused as a type mismatch.
Hold anything the scene must see for well over a second on OPC UA: an
S7-1500 forces a 1000 ms publishing interval on subscriptions, which is why the
driver polls by default.
